title: E2E latency trajectory needlemap and stage jacobian
summary: Working notes from a cross-team profiling session that built a 'needlemap' visualization (textual here) of per-stage latency trajectories across p50/p95/p99 for targeted cohorts. Goal: isolate dominant contributors to the E2E p99 tail and propose low-risk mitigations for the next sprint.
content:
Context:
- Problem: customer reports intermittent >1s responses (p99) for small-to-medium prompts on Dedicated clusters even though p50 is ~70ms.
- Scope: e2e traces collected 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-07, sample = 120,412 traces (stratified). Hardware mix: H100-prod (48%), A100-prod (39%), CPU-proxy (13%). Models: redwood-v2-small-ish and community/llama-variants.

Sampling & instrumentation notes:
- Traces sampled at ingress with full per-stage timestamps: tokenization.start/finish, serialize.start/finish, queue.enter/leave, batch.coalesce.start/finish, model.exec.start/finish, kv.lookup.start/finish (local vs remote), attention.kv-miss.fetch, postprocess.start/finish, egress.send.
- We enriched traces with: sequence_length_bucket (0-128,129-512,513-1024,>1024), coldstart_flag (true if node uptime < 60s), tenant_tier (free/paid/dedicated), batch_size_at_exec, backend_cpu_loadpct_at_exec.
- Sampling bias: we oversampled >1024 seqlen by 2x to ensure tail behavior.

High-level E2E quantiles (all traces):
- p50 = 78 ms
- p95 = 236 ms
- p99 = 822 ms

Needlemap: per-stage median and tail contributions (cohort: seq_len 129-512, warm nodes, batch size <=4)
Stage                  | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | % of p99
-----------------------|----------|----------|----------|--------
tokenize               | 4        | 6        | 9        | 1%
serialize              | 2        | 5        | 12       | 1%
queue.wait             | 8        | 22       | 110      | 13%
batch.coalesce         | 12       | 34       | 280      | 34%
model.exec             | 36       | 112      | 360      | 44%
kv.remote.fetch        | 0 (typ)  | 8        | 50       | 6%
postprocess/egress     | 6        | 16       | 91       | 6%

Observations (raw):
1) Batch coalesce and model.exec together account for ~78% of p99 in this cohort (12ms + 36ms p50 vs 280ms + 360ms p99).
2) The batch.coalesce p99 spread is multimodal: a cluster near 100-200ms and a tail 300-800ms. Correlates: concurrent GC events on proxy processes and high kernel-level futex contention between coalescer threads (trace annotations).
3) Model.exec long tail correlates strongly with two orthogonal signals: (a) increased backend_cpu_loadpct_at_exec (>85%), and (b) seq_len >512 combined with batch_size >8 for some misrouted traces.
4) queue.wait spikes align with transient slot exhaustion on XPU pools (observed in cluster telemetry) and with preemptible maintenance windows (rare).
5) KV remote fetch is not dominant for this cohort but explains a non-negligible fraction for >1024 sequences where local KV misses increase.

Hypotheses (ranked):
H1: Batch coalesce thread contention due to a shared lock on the coalescing priority queue causes long pauses under bursty arrival patterns.
H2: Model.exec tail is primarily scheduling/backpressure from noisy neighbors on shared GPU hosts when autoscaler triggers packing mixed tenants.
H3: A subset of traces are misrouted to a compatibility-mode runtime (slower quantized path) due to model variant mapping regression, adding 2-3x to exec time.
H4: Coldstarts account for a small p99 fraction but not the dominant mass for this cohort.

Quick checks performed (what we already ran):
- Replayed 5k sample traces in a staging cluster with tracing enabled; reproduced the multimodal coalesce tail.
- Heatmap of coalesce.wait vs arrival burstiness shows a strong positive correlation (Pearson r = 0.71).
- Pod-level profiling (perf + eBPF) on one offender captured ~30% time blocked in pthread_mutex_lock near coalesce queue pop.
- Verified routing logs: 2.4% of p99 traces for model X were served by quantized-compat runtime in last 7 days.

Immediate mitigation candidates (low-risk, quick):
- A1: Short-term: fall back to a lock-free ring buffer in the coalescer for small batch sizes (engineering spike: INF-EDGE-PR 1910). Owner: Ava. Risk: moderate.
- A2: Add admission control bursts smoothing at ingress (token-bucket shaping per-node) to reduce microbursts that trigger coalesce lock contention. Owner: Kai. Risk: low.
- A3: Add runtime check to avoid misrouting to compatibility-mode for high-velocity tenants (safety rule). Owner: Rohan. Risk: low.

Longer-term (perf goals for Q2):
- L1: Implement cooperative coalescing (per-core queues + batch-stealing) to eliminate global lock. Mech design doc required. Owner: infra team.
- L2: Improve autoscaler/placement affinity to avoid noisy-neighbor packing during critical SLO windows. Tie to Dedicated placement policy. Owner: platform-engineering.
- L3: Cache-aware model exec prefetching for >1024 sequences to reduce kv.remote.fetch amplification.

Experiment plan (next 3 sprints):
Sprint 1 (2 weeks):
- Run A2 (ingress shaping) on 10% of production traffic (canary) and track p95/p99 for coalesce and model.exec. Metric: p99 reduction >= 20% in canary. Linked ticket: JIRA-INF-4721.
- Patch to add quantized-runtime routing guard (A3). Verify via synthetic traffic.

Sprint 2 (3 weeks):
- Engineering spike for lock-free coalescer prototype in staging. Load test with arrival burst simulator.
- Telemetry: add coalesce.queue_depth_histogram and futex contention metric to tracing span.

Sprint 3 (4 weeks):
- If spike successful, roll out ring-buffer coalescer to 25% canary. Track CPU overhead and p99.
- Coordinate with autoscaler team to run placement experiments (noisy-neighbor avoidance).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: Is there a measurable CPU overhead tradeoff for lock-free ring buffer under steady-state throughput? (perf benchmark needed).
- Q2: For the traces misrouted to compatibility-mode, is the upstream model mapping service returning stale config or do we have concurrent rollout bugs? Need to audit model-mapping logs.
- Q3: Can we add a low-overhead 'preflight' that detects likely long sequences and pre-allocate KV slots to avoid remote fetch path?

Action items (owners):
- Rohan: Create INF-EDGE-PR tracker, draft design for admission shaping and routing guard. Due: 2026-03-06.
- Ava: Prototype lock-free coalescer spike. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Kai: Deploy ingress shaping canary and monitor dashboard. Due: 2026-03-09.
- Emily: Run placement experiment with platform-engineering and collect cohort-level p99 breakdown. Due: 2026-03-23.

Appendix (raw queries and dashboards):
- elastic search query used to pull traces: (index=traces-2026-02-*) AND service=serving-runtime AND model in (redwood-v2-small, community/llama) | sample stratified by seq_len_bucket
- perf script: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tools/trace-replay/replay.py --sample-file traces_02_01_07.json --client-threads 64
- Dashboards: Dash ID: D-serve-e2e-latency (internal), Panel: Stage breakdown by quantile, Panel: Coalesce lock contention (perf events).

Notes to self: keep this doc as the working source for the needlemap viz prototype. When we have coalescer spike results, move summary to a short executive brief for product and CS (impact numbers, customer examples).

Unresolved: collect customer examples (ticket ids) where p99 > 500ms and map to dedicated clusters vs hosted API (to prioritize Dedicated rollout fixes).

-- end of working notes --
